CHAPTER.VERS: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
How long ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.
Why are we counted as beasts, reputed vile in your sight?

He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of its place?
himself: Heb. his soul
Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.

The light shall be dark in his tent, and his lamp shall be put out with him.
candle: or, lamp
The steps of his strength shall be shortened, and his own counsel shall cast him down.
For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.
The trap shall take by the heel, the robber shall prevail against him.

The snare
laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.
laid: Heb. hidden

Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet.
drive: Heb. scatter

His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction
ready at his side.

It shall devour the strength of his skin: the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.
strength: Heb. bars
His confidence shall be rooted out of his tent, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.
It shall dwell in his tent, because none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.
The remembrance of him shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.

He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
He…: Heb. They shall drive him
He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.

They that come after shall be appalled at his day, as they that went before were seized with horror.
went…: or, lived with him
were…: Heb. laid hold on horror

Surely such the dwellings of the wicked, and this the place
knoweth not God.
